Multivariate Student-t family for several continuous responses

Source: R/families.R
mvt.Rd

mvn() with heavy-tailed residuals. Given the latent factors, each row follows a Student-t distribution with location mu, scale Psi and degrees of freedom nu, which every component shares. An outlying row then pulls less on the fit. The residual covariance is Z Z' + diag(Psi^2 * nu / (nu - 2)). A unit's responses do not follow a multivariate Student-t law. Their factors stay normal.

Usage

mvt()

Value

A family object to pass to jsdgam() or mvgam().

Details

nu is bounded below by 2, which keeps the residual variance finite. Its prior is gamma(2, 0.1), as brms gives a Student-t nu. Above the bound it places the median of nu at 17 and 95% of its mass between 3.2 and 56. prior(..., class = nu) and prior(..., class = Psi) set other priors. The data layout, the fit and the bound on n_lv follow mvn().

References

Hui, F. K. C., Taskinen, S., Pledger, S., Foster, S. D. and Warton, D. I. (2015). Model-based approaches to unconstrained ordination. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 6(4):399-411. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12236

See also

Other observation families: beta_nb(), categ(), com_binomial(), diri(), multi(), mvgam_families, mvn(), nmix(), occ(), tweedie()

Examples

# \dontrun{
simdat <- sim_jsdgam(family = mvt(), n_species = 5L, n_sites = 80L,
                     n_lv = 2L, seed = 1L)
fit <- jsdgam(
  formula        = y ~ env * series,
  factor_formula = ~ -1,
  data           = simdat$data_train,
  unit           = time, species = series,
  family         = mvt(),
  n_lv           = 2L,
  chains         = 2L,
  silent         = 2
)
#> Warning: 2 of 2 chains had an E-BFMI less than 0.3.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# The degrees of freedom, against 5 in the simulation
posterior_summary(fit, variable = "nu")
#>    Estimate Est.Error     Q2.5    Q97.5
#> nu 7.496331  4.557953 3.281795 18.84507
# }
